title: Meet a living Chatticus organization on the marketing site
description:
As a technical leader evaluating Chatticus, I want the marketing site to make the product and its named teammates immediately understandable, so that I can decide whether this controlled agent organization fits my work.

Feature: Living Chatticus marketing experience

  Scenario: A visitor understands the promise above the fold
    Given a visitor opens chattic.us
    When the marketing page finishes loading
    Then the hero says that Chatticus is an AI organization the visitor controls
    And it introduces persistent named teammates as visible characters
    And it offers a clear path to explore the product and source

  Scenario: A visitor understands how the organization works
    Given a visitor continues through the marketing page
    When they explore the product story
    Then they see one shared computer inside a boundary they control
    And they see skills, routines, review, and approval as distinct capabilities
    And they see that teammate motion reflects meaningful work states

  Scenario: A visitor can evaluate trust without invented proof
    Given the product is under active development
    When the visitor reviews evidence and comparisons
    Then shipped capabilities are distinguished from intended capabilities
    And no fabricated customer testimonial or adoption metric is presented
    And referenced third-party facts include source links

  Scenario: A visitor uses a narrow or reduced-motion display
    Given the visitor uses a phone or prefers reduced motion
    When the marketing page finishes loading
    Then all primary content remains readable without horizontal scrolling
    And essential meaning does not depend on animation
    And motion that is not essential is reduced or removed.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Specification milestone: added features/chatticus_brand_experience.feature and ran the focused Behave feature before production changes. It is red for the intended reason: five scenarios and twenty-five steps are undefined. The implementation will make these observable marketing and workspace behaviors pass.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Marketing implementation now presents Editor, Reporter, Copy Writer, and Illustrator as visibly distinct original Lottie characters through Vultus. Five marketing tests, production build, audits, desktop/mobile QA, reduced-motion checks, and frame-level model inspection passed locally. The site is not deployed and the change has not landed, so this story stays in progress.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Post-rebase marketing validation remains green. The new marketing stack is not deployed; its first deployment must resolve existing chattic.us and www.chattic.us CloudFront alias ownership. This story stays in progress until the change lands.

comments.author: home
comments.text: User review after seeing the app: marketing still feels too restrained, the current orbit mark reads as a solar-system logo, and bot/UI motion is not visually prominent. Expanding this story with a large motion showcase, more obvious role activity, kinetic handoffs, and a non-orbital wordmark mark before closing.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Hero direction revised from the user review: the primary visual is now a compact, interactive mobile workspace prototype rather than a large roster abstraction. It shows the named Editor, Reporter, Copy Writer, and Illustrator in their actual workspace context, with motion and live handoffs; the former orbital-looking mark is replaced by a conversation-stack mark. Marketing lint, typecheck, production build, and 7 page tests pass.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Milestone update: the marketing hero now leads with a compact interactive mobile workspace prototype (rather than a viewport-filling roster), keeping the named Editor, Reporter, Copy Writer, and Illustrator visible in actual app context. The conversation-stack mark replaces the orbit motif. Seven landing-page tests, lint, typecheck, and production build are green. Source remains unmerged and not deployed, so the story remains in progress for the next design-review session.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Handoff-ready after independent re-review: the hero now presents a responsive mobile workspace prototype, exposes the four explicit roles in context, and offers a labelled pause/resume control that pauses CSS motion and the pinned Vultus Lottie avatars. Reviewer approved. Validation: marketing lint/typecheck/build plus 7 tests; workspace lint/typecheck plus 14 tests; Vultus 14 tests and production build.

comments.author: home
comments.text: User refinement: restore the bold tilted rounded color planes behind the hero workspace prototype, replacing the floating-dot treatment. Give the planes only subtle transform-based motion and preserve the existing pause/reduced-motion contract.

comments.author: home
comments.text: User confirmed the restored historical hero backing plane and asked for motion that is perceptible but very subtle. Refining only the transform animation; no layout or visual-language change.

comments.author: home
comments.text: User approved the restrained hero motion and requested a slightly more legible treatment: independently modulate the apparent width and height of both the lime backing rectangle and grey shadow rectangle with non-matching periods. Implement with transform scale for smooth composited animation, preserving pause/reduced-motion behavior.
